verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 46.30
verses.english: Linked Discourses 46.30

verses.pali: 3. Udāyivagga
verses.english: 3. With Udāyī

verses.pali: Udāyisutta
verses.english: With Udāyī

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sumbhesu viharati setakaṁ nāma sumbhānaṁ nigamo.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sumbhas, near the town of the Sumbhas named Sedaka.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Udāyī went up to the Buddha … and said to him:

verses.pali: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
verses.english: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

verses.pali: Yāva bahukatañca me, bhante, bhagavati pemañca gāravo ca hirī ca ottappañca.
verses.english: How helpful my fondness and respect for the Buddha have been, and my sense of conscience and prudence.

verses.pali: Ahañhi, bhante, pubbe agārikabhūto samāno abahukato ahosiṁ dhammena abahukato saṅghena.
verses.english: For when I was still a layman, I wasn’t helped much by the teaching or the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: So khvāhaṁ bhagavati pemañca gāravañca hiriñca ottappañca sampassamāno agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito.
verses.english: But when I considered my fondness and respect for the Buddha, and my sense of conscience and prudence, I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

verses.pali: Tassa me bhagavā dhammaṁ desesi:
verses.english: The Buddha taught me the Dhamma:

verses.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the disappearance of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā …pe…
verses.english: Such is feeling …

verses.pali: iti saññā …
verses.english: Such is perception …

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā …
verses.english: Such are choices …

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the disappearance of consciousness.’

verses.pali: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, suññāgāragato imesaṁ pañcupādānakkhandhānaṁ ukkujjāvakujjaṁ samparivattento ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ abbhaññāsiṁ.
verses.english: Then, while staying in an empty hut, I followed the churning of the five grasping aggregates. I truly understood: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

verses.pali: Dhammo ca me, bhante, abhisamito, maggo ca me paṭiladdho;
verses.english: I comprehended the teaching, sir, I acquired the path.

verses.pali: yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṁ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṁ:
verses.english: This, when developed and cultivated by me meditating in just such a way, will bring me to such a state that I will understand:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi.
verses.english: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

verses.pali: Satisambojjhaṅgo me, bhante, paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṁ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṁ:
verses.english: I acquired the awakening factors of mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi …pe…
upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo me, bhante, paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṁ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṁ:
verses.english: Each of these, when developed and cultivated by me meditating in just such a way, will bring me to such a state that I will understand:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi.
verses.english: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho me, bhante, maggo paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṁ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṁ:
verses.english: This is the path that I acquired which, when developed and cultivated by me meditating in just such a way, will bring me to such a state that I will understand:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmī”ti.
verses.english: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: “Sādhu sādhu, udāyi.
verses.english: “Good, good, Udāyī!

verses.pali: Eso hi te, udāyi, maggo paṭiladdho, yo te bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṁ tathattāya upanessati yathā tvaṁ:
verses.english: For that is indeed the path that you acquired which, when developed and cultivated by you meditating in just such a way, will bring you to such a state that you will understand:

verses.pali: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā’ti pajānissasī”ti.
verses.english: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’”

verses.pali: Dasamaṁ.
Udāyivaggo tatiyo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Bodhāya desanā ṭhānā,
ayoniso cāparihānī;
Khayo nirodho nibbedho,
ekadhammo udāyināti.
